required_observations.description: The conversation begins with a public-launch and logo-use decision.

evidence.speaker: user
evidence.quote: Should we launch publicly and use its logo to attract other customers?

required_observations.description: The current question changes from whether to launch to what evidence should gate announcement.

evidence.speaker: user
evidence.quote: What evidence should we require before announcing?

required_observations.description: The user corrects the commitment assumption.
Only two friendly emails support the prospect-interest claim.

evidence.speaker: user
evidence.quote: We only have two friendly emails from their innovation lead

required_observations.description: The only senior engineer is already supporting existing customers.

evidence.speaker: user

required_observations.description: Board excitement is tied to the prospect's name.

evidence.speaker: user
evidence.quote: the board is excited mainly because of the company's name

required_observations.description: The user challenges treating interest as purchase commitment.

evidence.speaker: user
evidence.quote: I am worried we are treating their interest as a purchase commitment

required_observations.description: The user also wants to preserve the opportunity cost of waiting.

evidence.speaker: user
evidence.quote: I am also worried that waiting will make us lose the opportunity

required_observations.description: The assistant initially commits to a public beta and flagship partner framing.

evidence.speaker: assistant
evidence.quote: I would announce a limited public beta and make this prospect the flagship design partner.

required_observations.description: The assistant narrows implementation but does not reverse the public-launch direction.

evidence.speaker: assistant
evidence.quote: Keep the beta limited to three companies, avoid promising a service-level agreement, and use the announcement to test demand.

required_observations.description: Email confirmation becomes the only explicit pre-announcement threshold.

evidence.speaker: assistant
evidence.quote: Ask the prospect to confirm participation by email, then announce a 30-day beta next month.

required_observations.description: Detailed success criteria are deferred until after launch.

evidence.speaker: assistant
evidence.quote: You can define detailed success criteria after the first week once you see actual usage.

required_observations.description: The board's prestige-driven excitement is not integrated as an evidence problem.

evidence.speaker: user
evidence.quote: the board is excited mainly because of the company's name

required_observations.description: The purchase-commitment concern receives only an email-confirmation response and remains under-carried.

evidence.speaker: user
evidence.quote: I am worried we are treating their interest as a purchase commitment

required_observations.description: The direct request for an evidence standard is not answered with a substantive evidence set.

explicit_unresolved_or_absent.description: Permission to use the prospect's logo is not established.
No explicit stop or reversal rule appears before the audit.
Engineering capacity is acknowledged but not converted into an action gate.
No private or staged validation path is considered before the audit.
The user changes the question and adds counter-pressure but does not clearly change their mind.
